The arithmetic is off, though: `-resize 80%` scales each dimension, so 0.8^5 ≈ 33% is the linear factor and byte size falls closer to 0.64^5 ≈ 11%.

downsize_instructions_animated delegates to resize_instructions_animated, which interpolates the dimensions argument into `gifsicle --resize-fit #{dimensions}`. --resize-fit takes a WxH geometry (gifsicle spells percentage scaling --scale), so `--resize-fit 80%` is rejected; the non-zero exit makes convert_with return false, which this caller ignores. Every other caller of resize/downsize passes real integer dimensions.
